module: D09-08 大型股vs小型股領導
purpose: Define Taiwan size leadership as a conditional relative-performance/participation state, not a permanent small-cap premium or assumed large-to-small lead-lag.

officialProxyFamilies.index: FTSE TWSE Taiwan 50 Total Return Index
officialProxyFamilies.universeSemantics: 50 largest eligible TWSE companies by full market value under index rules

officialProxyFamilies.index: FTSE TWSE Taiwan Mid-Cap 100 Total Return Index
officialProxyFamilies.universeSemantics: next 100 eligible companies by full market value outside Taiwan 50

officialProxyFamilies.index: TWSE TAIEX Small-Cap 300 Total Return Sub-Index

excludedPrimaryProxy: TIP Taiwan Pristine SAM-Cap Select 100 is not a pure size proxy because it also screens profitability, dividends, market attention, operating stability and revenue growth.
Do not use today's market-cap quantiles to reconstruct historical size portfolios without effective-dated market-cap/universe evidence.

concentrationControls: Taiwan50 vs Taiwan50-30%-capped difference when available

positiveMechanisms: Small/mid-cap outperformance with broad participation can describe risk-appetite diffusion beyond mega-caps.
Large-cap leadership can reflect global-liquidity, institutional concentration, index-weight and mega-cap earnings sensitivity.
A transition from large-only to mid/small confirmation may be a different state from simultaneous broad weakness or a one-day small-cap bounce.
counterevidence: Taiwan historical research does not support a universal positive large-to-small lead-lag; strong contemporaneous correlations complicate causal interpretation.

Recent Taiwan size-effect research attributes predictability partly to illiquidity and price-limit/limits-to-arbitrage effects, so size leadership can be a microstructure/liquidity state rather than pure information diffusion.
Index sector composition differs materially by size; a technology cycle can masquerade as a size effect.
Index rebalances and constituent migration mechanically alter exposure; use official index series for return state and effective-dated membership only when interpreting constituents.
Small-cap index performance can be more volatile/less liquid; after-cost stock-selection implications must not be inferred from index spread alone.

pitClocks.returnObservation: official end-of-day total return index value after close
pitClocks.firstEligibleDecision: next decision point after official EOD value is available
pitClocks.membershipInterpretation: effective-dated index constituent/review state if constituent-level attribution is attempted
pitClocks.noHistoricalBackfillRule: Current constituents may not be backfilled to explain older index returns.

falsification: If size spread is explained by sector composition, classify SECTOR_MIX_DOMINATED rather than size leadership.
If small-cap relative strength disappears after liquidity/limit-hit controls, do not call it broad risk-on.
If relative return improves while small-cap breadth weakens, classify concentration/divergence rather than confirmation.
If only one horizon or one hand-picked index pair works, reject for horizon/index selection snooping.
No state receives a permanent bullish/bearish sign before prospective/OOS strategy interaction tests.
promotionReason: Official Taiwan large-, mid- and small-cap index families have explicit size semantics and official historical/end-of-day values, while Taiwan-specific literature supplies strong falsification against universal lead-lag and unconditional size-premium interpretations. Both mechanism/falsification and Taiwan PIT source feasibility are established; predictive value remains untested.

Add sector-mix/liquidity/limit-hit/volatility controls before any System1/System2 use.
Do not create a small-cap bonus or a fixed risk-on score.
